newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel up on dollar, weaker vs basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel up on dollar, weaker vs basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose mildly against the dollar but weakened slightly against the basket of foreign currencies amid conversions of foreign currency for end-of-the-month payments, dealers said.

"The market was quiet today. The business sector was converting foreign currency into shekels for end-of-the-month payments. The Bank of Israel had to intervene several times to support the basket," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"The representative rate for the basket was set at 6.97 percent below the slope. But after the setting of the representative rate the dollar and basket traded at a lower level," he said.

The shekel can trade in a band of seven percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1710 against 3.1730 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5541 shekels against 3.5532 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8774 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8911 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.1019 shekels per mark against 2.0967 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1695 shekels.
